tasks.short: Investigate employment practices and alleged discrimination, establish findings, and agree corrective action.

steps.what: Review the issue brief and set investigation scope.
Collect relevant employment records from the {HCM} and {ATS}.
Reconstruct events from records and verified interview notes.

loop.input: Authorised evidence records and verified interview notes.
loop.output: Source-linked chronology and allegation-by-evidence matrix, preserving conflicting accounts.
loop.check: Validate record identifiers and dates; officer checks attribution, omissions and disputed facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per document; unreadable or unresolved material goes to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative accounts describe events and contradictions without consistent fields.

steps.what: Compare documented practices against approved criteria in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess alternative explanations and determine findings.
Agree corrective actions, accountable roles and review dates.

tasks.design: Use a restricted case register in the {WORKFLOW}, with scoped record collection from the {HCM}, {ATS} and {DOCS}. Deterministic checks produce practice comparisons, while a bounded extraction loop drafts a source-linked chronology for officer approval. People determine findings and corrective action; approved aggregate results can feed a disclosure-controlled {BI} view of recurring barriers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fragmented records, inconsistent case identifiers and narrative evidence made preparation expensive. Investigative judgement also discouraged automating separable administrative work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing access controls, exports and workflow features can support the case register. AI-assisted coding reduces integration effort, and bounded extraction can prepare narrative evidence for review.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete records, credible competing accounts and disputed comparison groups remain difficult. GDPR requirements, relevant EU AI Act provisions and national rules constrain sensitive data use.
tasks.human_edge: The officer tests explanations, recognises power imbalances and makes defensible findings without treating statistical differences as proof.

ambition.what: Monthly review of recurring recruitment barriers using approved aggregate findings.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time collecting records and rebuilding timelines, and more time testing explanations and following corrective action. Investigation and employment decision rights remain unchanged; a recurring barrier review requires an explicit management mandate.

reach.task: Investigate whether job evaluation criteria create unequal outcomes.
reach.learn: Job evaluation methods, valid comparison groups and the limits of pay comparisons.

evidence.claim: Restricted records, deterministic comparisons and reviewed narrative extraction are plausible building blocks; the digest supplies no direct investigation case.
GDPR Article 22 is relevant if a future design makes solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
AI used for worker evaluation can fall within the EU AI Act employment high-risk categories; intended use needs assessment.

assumptions: A mid-size employer assigns this work to an HR compliance officer, sometimes with external legal support.
Time shares are planning estimates guided by the supplied priors, not observed measurements.
Collection follows an officer-defined scope and existing access entitlements.
The comparison engine flags differences and missing evidence; it does not decide discrimination.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and consultation work, not guaranteed statutory waiting periods.
unknowns: Countries, applicable national rules and employee representation arrangements.
Available interfaces, case identifiers and access to historical employment records.
Lawful bases and applicable conditions for processing special-category data.
Existing retention schedules, legal holds and investigation independence arrangements.
Who can authorise corrective action and recurring aggregate reviews.
research_questions: Which comparison checks can be specified without inferring protected characteristics?
What sampling method detects omitted or misattributed evidence?
Does the proposed processing require a DPIA or employee consultation under applicable rules?
new_work: Review extracted chronology and evidence attribution.
Resolve missing records and access failures.
Maintain comparison criteria, permissions and source mappings.
Check aggregate outputs for disclosure risk.
Track whether corrective actions address the identified barrier.

tasks.short: Prepare and release evidence-based reports on equal opportunity investigations.

steps.what: Assemble approved findings, evidence references and corrective actions.
Draft the investigation report using the approved template.

loop.input: Approved source pack and report template.
loop.output: Draft report with source references and explicit unresolved points.
loop.check: Require approved finding identifiers and valid citations; reject unsupported facts and changed conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per section; failed sections remain marked for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: The report must explain case-specific narrative evidence; fixed fields alone cannot produce that account.

steps.what: Check evidence, reasoning, confidentiality and proposed redactions.
Approve the report and its audience-specific disclosure scope.
Release approved report versions and file the disclosure record.

tasks.design: A generator assembles approved case material from the {DOCS} into a fixed report structure, with a bounded loop drafting explanatory sections. The officer reviews evidence and redactions, and the {WORKFLOW} binds release approval to the exact version, recipients and disclosure scope. Approved versions are released through the {DOCS} or {EMAIL}, with a disclosure log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report preparation mixed copying, narrative writing and substantive review in one document. Evidence references and approved versions were hard to keep aligned.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, version controls and approval flows already support deterministic assembly and release. Bounded drafting can turn approved findings into readable prose without reopening the investigation.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent report can conceal unsupported reasoning or inappropriate disclosure. Privilege, contested conclusions and audience-specific redaction require experienced review.
tasks.human_edge: The officer ensures the report explains the evidence fairly, preserves uncertainty and supports conclusions that can withstand challenge.
tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time assembling and formatting reports and more time checking reasoning and disclosure. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence-based briefing for a formal employment dispute.
reach.learn: Procedural fairness, disclosure duties and applicable national employment rules.

evidence.claim: Template assembly, source-linked drafting and version-bound release are proposed design patterns, not a documented equal opportunity reporting case.
The digest documents a report containing invented sources, supporting explicit citation checks and substantive review.

assumptions: Findings are approved upstream; report generation does not create new findings.
An investigation lead can authorise release without a conflict of interest.
A secure case register and approved evidence references are available.
Build ranges describe an incremental reporting module on that shared foundation.
Time shares are estimates; extensive legal review could materially change them.
unknowns: Required report formats, languages and external filing obligations.
Who approves reports when the complaint concerns senior HR staff.
Applicable privilege, access, disclosure and retention arrangements.
Whether existing document controls support audience-specific versions.
Whether new processing requires consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can each generated factual statement be traced to an approved source?
Which report sections can use fixed wording without a model?
Can release controls prevent stale approvals from authorising changed versions?
new_work: Check generated statements against evidence and approved findings.
Maintain templates and source-reference rules.
Review redactions and exact recipient lists.
Handle failed citations and missing source material.
Maintain release and disclosure records.

tasks.short: Interview complaint participants and witnesses to verify case information.

steps.what: Prepare neutral questions from the issue brief and evidence gaps.

loop.input: Issue brief, authorised evidence gaps and approved interview protocol.
loop.output: Neutral question guide linked to issues and gaps.
loop.check: Officer checks relevance, leading language, unsupported premises and participant-specific sensitivities.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per guide; officer writes unresolved questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case-specific gaps need questions that cannot all be selected from a fixed checklist.

steps.what: Arrange a confidential interview and confirm accessibility needs.
Conduct the interview, explore inconsistencies and record contemporaneous notes.
Organise notes into attributed statements and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Officer's contemporaneous notes and interview guide.
loop.output: Attributed draft record distinguishing statements, quotations and officer observations.
loop.check: Officer compares every substantive statement with the notes; no reconstructed quotations or credibility scores.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; ambiguous passages retain the original wording for manual resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-form notes lack consistent structure and may contain several speakers or unresolved references.

steps.what: Resolve factual corrections with the participant and finalise the interview record.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} coordinates confidential invitations through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, including requests for suitable interview arrangements. Bounded loops prepare question guides and organise officer-written notes in the {DOCS}, subject to officer approval. Interviews and factual clarification remain human conversations, with no recording required.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling and note preparation were embedded in a sensitive conversation process. Generic forms could not adapt questions to conflicting accounts.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling controls and reusable interview protocols handle routine coordination. Bounded drafting can assist preparation and paperwork while the officer conducts the interview.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, trauma, interpretation and power imbalances require skilled handling. Accessibility arrangements and participant corrections can require substantial individual work.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer creates conditions for candid testimony, follows unexpected evidence and distinguishes uncertainty from inconsistency.

ambition.what: Employees unable to use the standard interview format because they need interpretation or accessibility support.

tasks.altitude: The officer has more preparation time and can arrange suitable interview formats earlier. Authority over findings and employment outcomes does not change.

reach.task: Conduct a procedurally fair grievance interview.
reach.learn: Representation rights, trauma-aware questioning and interpreter practice under applicable national rules.

evidence.claim: Interview preparation and paperwork can be assisted independently of the human conversation; no direct interview automation case is supplied.
The EU AI Act prohibits workplace emotion recognition, subject to narrow medical or safety exceptions; this design uses none.

assumptions: Interviews are normally conducted by a trained officer through a confidential meeting or call.
Contemporaneous notes are available; automatic recording and transcription are outside this design.
Participant verification records corrections and disagreement, rather than implying agreement with investigative findings.
The supplied human-work prior is retained: conversation remains the largest time component.
The shared restricted case store is available; interpreter services are separate operating costs.
unknowns: Existing interview protocols and participant verification practices.
Required representation, accompaniment and interpreter arrangements under national rules.
Which employees currently cannot access the standard interview format.
Approved channels for invitations and participant corrections.
Consultation requirements for introducing model-assisted handling of interview notes.
research_questions: Do generated guides preserve neutral wording across complaint types?
Can note organisation preserve uncertainty and attribution without adding meaning?
Which interview formats best support employees with different accessibility needs?
new_work: Review question guides for neutrality and unsupported premises.
Check organised notes against the original record.
Coordinate interpretation and accessibility support.
Manage participant corrections and disputed wording.
Maintain confidential scheduling templates and access permissions.

tasks.short: Review equal opportunity complaints, clarify allegations, and define the issues requiring investigation.

steps.what: Register the complaint and attachments received through the {EMAIL}.
Read the complaint and identify allegations, dates, people and missing information.

loop.output: Source-linked allegations, stated dates, named roles and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Officer checks completeness, attribution and distinction between allegations and established facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per complaint; unreadable material and uncertainty go to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Complaints use varied narrative language and often mix events, interpretations and requested outcomes.

steps.what: Check relevant policies, procedural deadlines and available referral routes.
Clarify events, desired outcomes and immediate concerns with the complainant.
Define investigation issues and determine urgent escalation or referral.

tasks.design: Configure confidential intake in the {WORKFLOW}, with complaint material held in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop drafts an allegation map, and deterministic rules prepare a checklist from approved procedures and confirmed dates. The officer clarifies the complaint, determines urgent routing and produces the issue brief used by the investigation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaints arrived as inconsistent narratives and attachments. Procedural checks were mixed with sensitive interpretation and personal clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable intake can establish consistent records, and a small extraction loop can structure narrative material. Versioned rules can handle known procedural requirements without a model interpreting the law.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous allegations, urgent protection needs and overlapping procedures resist fixed rules. National employment rules and changing procedural guidance require qualified maintenance.
tasks.human_edge: The officer notices what the complainant struggles to express, identifies immediate concerns and frames issues without prejudging the complaint.
tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time locating facts and checking routine procedural details, leaving more time for clarification. Routing and investigation decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Triage employee grievances into appropriate procedures.
reach.learn: Grievance boundaries, urgent escalation criteria and neutral issue framing.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, reviewed allegation extraction and deterministic procedural checklists are feasible patterns; no direct complaint-triage case is supplied.
GDPR Article 22 supports checking significant automated decision risks; the proposed system does not reject or close complaints automatically.
Dutch national rules include works council consent rights concerning specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; other countries require separate assessment.

assumptions: Complaints commonly arrive through a confidential mailbox or equivalent internal channel.
Procedural rules are approved by qualified staff before encoding.
Unknown dates produce an unresolved checklist item rather than a calculated definitive deadline.
No model infers protected characteristics, assesses credibility or decides complaint admissibility.
The supplied priors inform time estimates, while clarification and issue framing remain substantial human work.
Build ranges include a restricted intake foundation that the other task modules can reuse.
unknowns: Complaint channels, volume, languages and attachment formats.
Applicable countries, procedures, deadlines and employee consultation arrangements.
Existing lawful bases, special-category processing conditions and privacy notices.
Who handles conflicts of interest and immediate protection concerns.
Whether approved model processing is permitted for complaint material.
research_questions: Which procedural rules are genuinely deterministic across the applicable countries?
How reliably does extraction retain secondary allegations and uncertain dates?
What fail-safe escalation route works when the usual recipient has a conflict?
new_work: Review allegation maps for omissions and premature conclusions.
Maintain versioned procedure and deadline rules.
Resolve uncertain dates, duplicate records and unreadable attachments.
Review permissions and confidential routing.
Evaluate missed issues using a representative sample of completed cases.

role.altitude: The role shifts from assembling case material towards testing evidence, conducting sensitive conversations and checking whether corrective actions work. Findings, disclosures and employment decisions remain accountable human responsibilities; broader review authority requires a management mandate.
reach: Support labor relations specialists with fair interview records and evidence-based dispute briefings.
Help compensation and benefits specialists examine job evaluation barriers using valid comparison groups.
Help HR specialists route grievances consistently while preserving confidential escalation.
skills_to_grow: Evidence provenance, contradiction analysis and source checking.
Comparison-group design and limits of aggregate statistics.
GDPR safeguards, relevant EU AI Act requirements and applicable national rules.
Workflow configuration, access controls and procedural rule maintenance.
Evaluating model omissions and unsupported narrative claims.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a monthly, disclosure-controlled review of recurring recruitment barriers, connecting substantiated findings to specific policy changes and follow-up evidence. Keep individual complaint handling independent and require an explicit mandate for broader organisational review.
